heightpill-height-blackpill.summary: The forum belief that height drives a man's dating outcomes, which pushes people toward lifts, styling and other ways to look taller.

quick.overview:
The heightpill is the belief, common on looksmaxxing forums, that a man's height is one of the biggest factors in dating and social outcomes. For readers it works as a motivator: it points attention to looking taller through lifts, posture, tailoring and other height-adding choices.

Studies report that many women prefer taller male partners on average and that shorter men are rated less favourably. Other work finds people trade height against traits like income and education, and that preferences vary across cultures.
quick.how: It is a framework rather than a product. People who adopt it usually respond by working on the height they can influence: shoe lifts, posture, clothes cut to lengthen the frame, haircuts, and photo framing. Some look into more drastic height-altering measures covered in other entries.
quick.risks: The main documented concern is psychological distress among teens and men who fixate on height. The measures people reach for to change height carry their own medical risks, covered in those entries.

angle.text: Looksmaxxing forums use the heightpill to describe the belief that height strongly shapes a man's dating outcomes, which drives interest in lifts, styling and, for some, surgery. Research shows many women prefer taller partners on average, with the preference varying by culture and trading off against other traits.

mazdutide.summary: A weekly GLP-1 and glucagon dual-agonist injection, approved in China for weight loss, used to get leaner by cutting appetite and raising energy use.

quick.overview:
Mazdutide is a once-weekly injection that activates both GLP-1 and glucagon receptors, developed by Innovent and Eli Lilly. People interested in it want lower body fat and a leaner face and body.

The GLP-1 side reduces appetite and slows stomach emptying, while the glucagon side is proposed to raise energy expenditure. A phase 3 placebo-controlled trial in Chinese adults with obesity or overweight reported clinically relevant weight loss, and it was approved for weight management in China in June 2025. Trials measured weight, not appearance.
quick.how: It is a prescription medicine in China, taken as a weekly injection under medical supervision. Elsewhere it is still investigational, and it appears in fat-loss discussions as a possible next-generation option. Weight loss builds over weeks to months of use, and users typically pair it with diet changes and training.
quick.risks: Trials describe gastrointestinal side effects typical of GLP-1 drugs. It is prescription-only in China and investigational elsewhere, so access outside approved markets means unregulated supply. Trial participants have mostly been Chinese adults.

angle.text: Fat-loss-focused users look to mazdutide, a weekly GLP-1 and glucagon dual agonist, for lower body fat and a leaner look. It reduces appetite and is proposed to raise energy use, and it is approved in China for weight loss, with trials measuring weight rather than appearance.

orforglipron.summary: A once-daily GLP-1 pill that is not a peptide, taken to cut appetite and body fat for a leaner look without injections.

quick.overview:
Orforglipron is a once-daily pill from Eli Lilly that activates the GLP-1 receptor without being a peptide, so no injection is needed. People look to it for appetite control and lower body fat, giving a leaner face and body.

It binds the GLP-1 receptor, which regulates appetite and food intake, so you eat less. Phase 2 and 3 trials in adults with obesity reported dose-related weight loss versus placebo over 72 weeks, and it is sold in the US as Foundayo for chronic weight management. Trials measured weight, not appearance.
quick.how: It is a prescription daily tablet used alongside diet and physical activity. As a pill it is an oral alternative to injectable GLP-1 drugs. Weight loss builds gradually over weeks to months.
quick.risks: Common effects are gastrointestinal. The label carries a boxed warning about thyroid C-cell tumours that applies to the GLP-1 class, and also warns about pancreatitis and kidney injury, and advises stopping in pregnancy. It is prescription-only.

angle.text: Fat-loss-focused users look to orforglipron, a once-daily GLP-1 pill, as an oral alternative to injectables for getting leaner. It lowers appetite and intake, and phase 3 trials have measured weight loss rather than appearance.

oral-semaglutide-rybelsus.summary: Semaglutide as a daily tablet that lowers appetite for fat loss; Rybelsus is approved for type 2 diabetes and a weight-loss version is approved in the US.

quick.overview:
Oral semaglutide is the tablet form of the GLP-1 drug semaglutide, sold as Rybelsus for type 2 diabetes. People discuss it as a no-injection route to lower body fat and a leaner look.

It activates GLP-1 receptors, which reduces appetite and affects blood sugar, and an absorption enhancer in the tablet helps the peptide survive the stomach. The FDA approved an oral semaglutide for weight management under the Wegovy name in December 2025. Trials measure weight rather than appearance.
quick.how: It is a prescription tablet taken daily and is discussed in fat-loss communities as an alternative to the weekly pens. As with other GLP-1 drugs, it is combined with diet changes, and results build over weeks to months.
quick.risks: Common effects are nausea, diarrhoea, vomiting and constipation. The label carries a boxed thyroid C-cell tumour warning, and it is contraindicated with certain thyroid cancer histories. It is prescription-only.

angle.text: Fat-loss-focused users look to oral semaglutide, a tablet form of the GLP-1 drug, to cut appetite and get leaner without injections. It is established for type 2 diabetes and a weight-loss version is approved, with trials measuring weight rather than appearance.

garcinia-cambogia.summary: A fruit-rind supplement rich in hydroxycitric acid, taken as an over-the-counter fat burner to get leaner.

quick.overview:
Garcinia cambogia is a tropical fruit whose rind contains hydroxycitric acid (HCA), sold as an over-the-counter fat-loss supplement. People take it hoping for lower body fat and a leaner look.

In the lab, HCA inhibits ATP-citrate lyase, an enzyme involved in making fatty acids, which is the basis for claims it reduces fat storage. A 1998 JAMA trial and later systematic reviews of weight-loss supplements describe limited or inconsistent effects on body weight; appearance has not been studied.
quick.how: It is taken as capsules or powders of the extract, often as part of a broader fat-loss stack alongside diet and exercise. It appears both on its own and in multi-ingredient blends.
quick.risks: Reported effects include nausea, stomach discomfort, headache and dry mouth. Liver toxicity has been reported with products containing the extract, mostly multi-ingredient blends, and it may interact with some medicines.

angle.text: Users take garcinia cambogia, sold for its hydroxycitric acid, as a fat burner to get leaner. The idea is that HCA slows fat production in cells; human trials and reviews have measured body weight and mostly report small effects.

raspberry-ketones.summary: The aroma compound of red raspberries, sold as a fat-burning supplement for a leaner look.

quick.overview:
Raspberry ketone is the main aroma molecule of red raspberries, widely used as a flavouring and in perfumery. Supplements, usually made synthetically, are marketed as fat burners for a leaner look.

Proponents say it boosts fat breakdown and raises adiponectin or norepinephrine signalling. Laboratory studies in obese rats have reported changes in lipid levels, insulin resistance and fat-tissue gene expression. Published human weight-loss trials are essentially absent.
quick.how: It is taken as capsules, often in multi-ingredient fat-burner blends alongside diet and exercise. Users typically stack it with other thermogenic supplements.
quick.risks: The FDA classed raspberry ketone as generally recognised as safe only as a food flavouring in tiny amounts, and supplement-level safety in people is poorly characterised. Case reports describe coronary vasospasm and ventricular tachycardia in people taking raspberry ketone weight-loss products, and a 2015 toxicology paper and a Danish university raised concerns.

angle.text: Supplement users take raspberry ketones as a fat burner, on the basis of cell and rat findings that suggest faster fat breakdown. Human weight-loss trials are essentially absent, so use rests mostly on those lab results and user reports.

conjugated-linoleic-acid-cla.summary: A fatty acid from ruminant meat and dairy, sold as a supplement to reduce body fat and support a leaner, more muscular look.

quick.overview:
Conjugated linoleic acids are fatty acids found mainly in meat and dairy from cattle and sheep. Supplements are sold for fat loss and as a bodybuilding aid, aimed at a leaner physique.

Interest began with late-1990s mouse experiments that reported large drops in body fat, linked to the t10,c12 isomer. Human trials have generally shown much smaller effects, and a 2012 meta-analysis found no long-term effect on body composition in overweight or obese people.
quick.how: It is taken as softgel capsules, usually within a cutting routine of diet and training. Products differ in isomer mix, and results in trials have been small or short-lived.
quick.risks: A 2018 meta-analysis of randomised trials reported that CLA supplementation may raise C-reactive protein and TNF-alpha, markers of inflammation. The US FDA categorised CLA as generally recognised as safe for use in foods in 2008. Long-term effects in humans remain under study.

angle.text: Users take CLA, a fatty acid found in ruminant meat and dairy, to shift fat storage and get leaner. Mouse studies reported large body-fat drops, while human trials measuring body composition report small or short-lived changes.

forskolin.summary: A Coleus forskohlii plant extract that raises cAMP in cells, taken as a fat burner for a leaner, more defined look.

quick.overview:
Forskolin is a compound from the roots of Coleus forskohlii, a plant used in Ayurvedic medicine. Supplement makers market the extract for fat loss and lean mass, so users can look leaner and more defined.

Forskolin directly activates adenylyl cyclase, which raises cAMP, and in fat cells raised cAMP is associated with fat breakdown. That cell effect is well established and is why it is a standard lab tool. Early human weight-loss studies were small, and they are described as low quality with inconclusive results.
quick.how: It is taken as capsules of Coleus extract, usually in a cutting routine alongside diet and training, and often stacked with other fat-burner ingredients.
quick.risks: Forskolin influences cAMP signalling in many tissues, including heart and blood vessels, and laboratory work has studied cardiovascular effects. Human safety data for long-term supplement use are limited.

angle.text: Users take forskolin, a Coleus forskohlii extract, as a fat burner to get leaner and sometimes to support body composition. It raises cAMP in cells, which is linked to fat breakdown, and the human studies on weight are small.

fucoxanthin.summary: A brown-seaweed pigment taken as a fat-burner supplement to reduce belly fat and get leaner.

quick.overview:
Fucoxanthin is an orange-brown carotenoid found in brown seaweeds such as wakame. Supplements, often seaweed or microalgae extracts, are sold for fat loss and metabolic health, with abdominal fat as the main target.

The pitch grows from rodent experiments, notably a 2005 study showing lower abdominal fat in animals fed lipids from Undaria pinnatifida, with higher expression of uncoupling protein 1 (UCP1) in white fat. Human data are limited to a few small trials, and studies indicate low bioavailability.
quick.how: It is taken as capsules of seaweed or microalgae extract, typically alongside diet and exercise. The compound is sensitive to light, heat and oxygen, so product quality varies.
quick.risks: Reviews report it to be well tolerated in animals, and seaweed has long been eaten as food. Human safety data for concentrated supplements are limited.

angle.text: Supplement users take fucoxanthin, a brown-seaweed pigment, to burn fat and cut abdominal fat. The idea comes from rodent studies in which it raised fat-burning protein activity in white fat; human data are limited and absorption appears low.

glucomannan.summary: A konjac fibre that swells into a gel in the stomach so you feel fuller and eat less while leaning out.

quick.overview:
Glucomannan is a soluble fibre from the konjac plant, used in shirataki noodles and sold as a supplement. Dieters take it to feel full on fewer calories while getting leaner.

It absorbs water and forms a viscous gel in the stomach, which proponents say increases fullness and slows nutrient absorption. A meta-analysis found a non-significant weight difference of about 0.22 kg versus placebo, while the EU has allowed a weight-loss claim since 2010 for people on calorie-restricted diets. A meta-analysis also suggests it may lower LDL cholesterol by up to 10 percent.
quick.how: It is taken as capsules, powder or in konjac foods before meals, always with plenty of fluid, as part of a calorie-controlled diet. Health Canada advises against taking it at bedtime.
quick.risks: Taken with too little water, glucomannan products can cause choking or bowel obstruction. Common effects are diarrhoea, belching and bloating. The US FDA barred konjac jelly candies from import in 2001 over choking hazards.

angle.text: Dieters take glucomannan, a konjac fibre that forms a gel in the stomach, to feel fuller and eat less while getting leaner. Meta-analyses of weight loss report small changes.

psyllium-husk.summary: Gel-forming fibre from Plantago seed husks that keeps you fuller between meals, making a calorie deficit and leaner look easier to hold.

quick.overview:
Psyllium is a soluble fibre from the seed coat of Plantago ovata, a long-standing over-the-counter supplement. Users take it to feel full between meals, so it is easier to hold a calorie deficit and lean out for a more defined face and body.

It is not absorbed in the small intestine; it absorbs water and forms a gel that adds bulk, and the fullness effect is attributed to the same gel. It is best studied for constipation, LDL cholesterol and blood sugar. A 2023 review reported minor weight loss over 12 weeks in people with overweight or obesity.
quick.how: It is mixed as a powder into water or taken as capsules, often before meals, with plenty of fluid, as part of a calorie-controlled diet. It is also used in baking as a thickener.
quick.risks: Common effects are gas, bloating and abdominal pain. With too little water it can thicken in the throat and cause choking or bowel obstruction. Allergic reactions including anaphylaxis occur, and ConsumerLab found lead in all nine psyllium supplements it tested in 2024.

angle.text: Users take psyllium fibre to feel fuller between meals, so it is easier to hold a calorie deficit and lean out for a more defined face and body. It is well studied for digestion and cholesterol, and weight-loss trials report small effects.

apple-cider-vinegar.summary: Fermented apple vinegar drunk diluted for appetite and fat loss and used as a skin toner and hair rinse.

quick.overview:
Apple cider vinegar is made by fermenting apple juice into alcohol and then acetic acid, about 5 percent of the liquid. In looksmaxxing circles it is drunk diluted for fat loss and appetite control, and used as a skin toner and hair rinse for clearer skin and shinier hair.

The active part is generally taken to be acetic acid, with proposed effects on slower stomach emptying and post-meal glucose and insulin. Small studies suggest modest effects on blood glucose and cholesterol. Reviews describe limited or poor-quality evidence for weight loss, and the Mayo Clinic is quoted as saying meaningful weight loss is unlikely. The topical uses rest on its acidity and lab antimicrobial activity.
quick.how: It is mixed into water and drunk, often before meals, or diluted for use as a toner or hair rinse. Gummies and tablets are also sold.
quick.risks: Reported problems include tooth enamel erosion, throat or esophageal injury from tablets, reflux and stomach upset, and skin burns or eye injury when used undiluted. It may interact with insulin and diuretics. Food amounts are generally regarded as safe by regulators.

angle.text: Apple cider vinegar is drunk diluted for appetite control and fat loss and used as a skin toner and hair rinse for clearer skin and shinier hair. Small trials exist on weight and blood sugar, while the skin and hair uses rest on its acidity and user reports.

green-coffee-bean-extract.summary: A chlorogenic-acid extract of unroasted coffee beans taken as a fat-loss pill for a leaner physique.

quick.overview:
Green coffee bean extract is made from unroasted coffee beans, which are rich in chlorogenic acid, a compound largely lost in roasting. It is sold in capsules as a fat-burning and appetite supplement for a leaner physique.

Chlorogenic acid is proposed to slow carbohydrate absorption and change fat and glucose metabolism, and mouse studies reported less fat accumulation. A 2011 meta-analysis found tentative weight-loss effects with poor-quality trials, and a 2017 review said human studies were too poor to draw conclusions. A widely cited 2012 trial was retracted in 2014, and the FTC took action against several marketers in 2014-2015. It has also been studied for blood pressure and metabolic markers.
quick.how: It is taken as capsules, usually standardised to chlorogenic acid, alongside diet and exercise. Products vary in chlorogenic acid content and sometimes contain caffeine.
quick.risks: Trials in people with mild hypertension reported blood pressure effects and no major adverse events in small samples. Products vary in strength and may contain caffeine. It is sold as a dietary supplement rather than a licensed drug.

angle.text: Users take green coffee bean extract, a chlorogenic-acid pill, as a fat burner aimed at a leaner physique. It has been studied for blood pressure and metabolic markers, and its best-known weight-loss trial was retracted.

chromium-picolinate.summary: A chromium supplement marketed to curb sugar cravings, cut fat and support muscle definition.

quick.overview:
Chromium picolinate is trivalent chromium bound to picolinic acid, sold as a supplement for weight loss, muscle building and blood sugar support. Forum interest centres on the claim that it reduces carbohydrate cravings, making it easier to cut fat and keep muscle definition.

Chromium is proposed to enhance insulin signalling, sometimes through a peptide called chromodulin. Insulin-receptor effects were seen in vitro but not adequately shown in living organisms. A 2013 Cochrane review found no reliable evidence on weight loss or muscle gain in overweight adults, and the European Food Safety Authority found insufficient evidence for a body-weight effect.
quick.how: It is taken as a daily capsule or tablet, often within a cutting or muscle-building routine, or in multi-ingredient fat-loss stacks.
quick.risks: Typical supplement amounts show little evidence of toxicity. Reported effects include allergic reactions, headache, insomnia and irritability, and rare case reports describe kidney or liver injury at high intakes. It may interact with insulin and other diabetes medicines.

angle.text: Chromium picolinate is marketed to curb sugar cravings, cut fat and support muscle development through steadier blood sugar. Reviews of body weight and lean mass report no reliable effects.

detox-slimming-teas.summary: Herbal teas, often senna-based, drunk to de-bloat and drop scale weight fast before events or photos.

quick.overview:
Detox or slimming teas are herbal blends marketed for cleansing and weight loss, and many rely on senna, a plant whose sennosides are a stimulant laxative. Users drink them to de-bloat and look flatter around the stomach for a short window, such as before an event or photos.

Senna increases fluid and electrolytes in the large bowel and stimulates gut movement, so the scale change largely reflects stool and water loss rather than body fat. A 2015 review of detox diets found no compelling evidence for weight management or toxin elimination, and weight lost on such regimens is typically regained.
quick.how: People brew the tea for a few days, often timed to an event. It is usually combined with lighter eating during that period.
quick.risks: Reported senna effects are abdominal cramps, diarrhea, nausea and flatulence, and lower potassium, which can increase digoxin toxicity. Regular use can cause melanosis coli, a brown discoloration of the colon wall. Senna is contraindicated in intestinal obstruction and some inflammatory bowel conditions.

angle.text: Users drink detox and slimming teas to de-bloat and drop scale weight quickly before events or photos. The change is typically fluid and gut contents rather than fat, and a 2015 review found no compelling evidence for detox claims.

laxatives-for-weight-loss.summary: Taking laxatives to drop scale weight and look flatter briefly; the change is mostly water and the practice is linked to eating disorders.

quick.overview:
Some people use over-the-counter laxatives to lower the number on the scale quickly and look flatter for a short time. The change is described as water-weight loss.

Laxatives act in the large intestine after nutrients have already been absorbed, so they mainly remove water and electrolytes rather than calories. A prospective study of 10,058 US women followed from 2001 to 2016 linked laxative and diet pill use for weight control to a later first eating-disorder diagnosis.
quick.how: People use it as a short-term scale-weight tactic, for example before a weigh-in or photo. Clinical literature classifies it as a purging behaviour associated with eating disorders, and eating-disorder services offer help.
quick.risks: Reported harms include dehydration, low blood pressure, electrolyte and acid-base disturbances that can be fatal, kidney damage and colonic problems. Laxative misuse is tied to anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa in clinical literature, and anyone struggling with it can seek support from an eating-disorder service.

angle.text: Some people take laxatives to drop scale weight and look flatter for a short time. The loss is mostly water rather than fat, and clinical literature classifies the behaviour as purging linked to eating disorders.

compounded-semaglutide-microdosing-glp-1.summary: Pharmacy-made or gray-market semaglutide, often used at below-label amounts, to cut appetite and body fat for a leaner face and body.

quick.overview:
Compounded semaglutide has the same active ingredient as Ozempic or Wegovy but is prepared by a compounding pharmacy instead of the manufacturer. Microdosing means using less than the label amount, a practice seen in fat-loss and longevity circles, with the aim of lower appetite and body fat and a leaner face and physique with fewer side effects or lower cost.

Semaglutide activates GLP-1 receptors, which lowers appetite and slows stomach emptying. Approved semaglutide has strong trial results for weight loss at labeled doses. For microdosed or compounded versions, evidence is limited to a narrative review and early-stage registered trials.
quick.how: People get it from compounding pharmacies, often as multi-dose vials, and use amounts below the approved label. It is combined with diet changes and training, and results build over weeks to months.
quick.risks: Common effects are nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain and constipation. The FDA does not review compounded drugs for safety or effectiveness and has reported adverse events linked to dosing errors, off-label dosing, unapproved salt forms, improper shipping and counterfeit products.

angle.text: Users take compounded or gray-market semaglutide, often at below-label amounts, to cut appetite and body fat for a leaner face and physique. Fat loss is established at approved doses in large trials, while the microdosing version has not been studied.

calorie-deficit-calorie-counting.summary: Eating below maintenance and logging it: the baseline way to lose fat and reveal jawline, cheekbones and abs.

quick.overview:
A calorie deficit means eating less energy than you burn, and calorie counting is tracking intake to keep that gap. It is the usual foundation of a cut in looksmaxxing circles, used to strip body fat and reveal jawline, cheekbones and abs.

When intake is below energy expenditure, the body draws on stored energy, mostly fat but also some lean tissue. Calorie restriction is well established to produce weight and fat loss. The intake best for health is not known, and there is little research on appearance outcomes specifically.
quick.how: People estimate maintenance calories, set a daily target below it, and log food with an app or scale, usually alongside resistance training and higher protein to hold muscle. Visible changes build over weeks to months.
quick.risks: Reported effects include cold sensitivity, hormonal and menstrual changes, and, in severe restriction as in the Minnesota experiment, muscle wasting, anemia and depression. Moderate restriction may be harmful for people who are already lean.

angle.text: A calorie deficit tracked by counting is the baseline method in looksmaxxing circles for cutting body fat to reveal jawline, cheekbones and abs. Fat loss from a deficit is well established, while research on facial appearance specifically is limited.

high-protein-diet.summary: Protein-forward eating that helps you keep muscle while cutting and stay full on fewer calories, for a leaner, fuller physique.

quick.overview:
A high-protein diet raises protein above the standard 0.8 g/kg allowance, mainly through meat, fish, eggs, dairy and legumes. It is popular for cutting and muscle building, to keep a muscular look while leaning out.

Protein increases satiety, has a higher thermic effect than carbohydrates or fat, and supplies amino acids for muscle repair. Higher intake is linked to more muscle and less muscle loss during energy deficits. Looksmaxxing communities also discuss it for hair and skin, claims that have not been tested.
quick.how: People build meals around a protein source, often hitting a daily target in the range of 1.2 to 2.0 g/kg when active, and add protein powder or shakes. It is paired with resistance training and a calorie deficit when cutting.
quick.risks: Reviews disagree on kidney risk at higher intakes, and people with kidney disease are advised to consult clinicians. Restrictive versions may cause constipation, headaches or bad breath, and the AHA has cautioned about diets high in saturated fat.

angle.text: Users eat protein-forward to hold onto muscle while dieting and to stay full on fewer calories, giving a leaner, more muscular look. Studies link higher intake to more muscle and less muscle loss in a deficit; the hair and skin claims have not been tested.

omad-one-meal-a-day.summary: Eating all daily food in one sitting, a simple way to run a calorie deficit and lean out.

quick.overview:
OMAD means one meal a day, usually in a one- to two-hour window. It is a form of intermittent fasting used to cut body fat and get a leaner look with one simple rule.

Compressing eating into one window tends to lower total daily intake, which produces a calorie deficit. Broader intermittent fasting research shows modest weight loss, with limited evidence that it outperforms continuous calorie restriction, and no trials specific to OMAD and appearance were found.
quick.how: People eat a single large meal and fast the rest of the day, drinking only calorie-free drinks. It is sometimes combined with low-carbohydrate eating or fat-loss drugs, and with resistance training to hold muscle.
quick.risks: Short-term hunger, irritability, dizziness and headaches are reported. Health bodies advise against intermittent fasting for pregnant women, children, older adults, underweight people and those with eating disorders.

angle.text: Users eat all daily food in one sitting as a simple way to run a calorie deficit and lean out. It is a form of time-restricted eating, and no trials have tested OMAD specifically for appearance.
